### <a id="b-091"></a>[🐞 B-091](#top)

**Windows: a fenced stop ends uncertain after a SQLite "disk I/O error" while recording it**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🔴 Open | 🔶 P2 | 🟡 Medium | 3 h agent + 0.25 h owner | — | [F-005-T29](#f-005-t29) | 🤖 | 🧑‍🔧 | — |

🧑 **→** B-091-T02: on Tabgha's desktop session, update NERV-02 and run one fenced stop ([page](acceptance/b091-tabgha-fenced-stop.md)).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Found 2026-11-18 on Tabgha (F-005-T24), from the desktop session: the fenced stop removed the task and ended NERV-02, then printed "disk I/O error" and left the receipt `uncertain` with `stop:started`. The disk was fine (115 GB free) and the lifecycle journal had been written at 18:43. Cause (named 2026-11-25): the stop's poll read the live database read-only with no busy handler while the killed `serve` left its WAL behind. A later stop on the same machine completed. |
| **Reproduce** | On Windows, a fenced stop of a running NERV service from the desktop session; intermittent (once in two stops). |
| **Check** | The failing write is named (journal and statement); a committed test fails first if the cause is in code (for example a retry on SQLITE_IOERR or BUSY while the stopped process releases the file); a fenced stop on Tabgha completes its receipt. |

### <a id="f-062"></a>[✨ F-062](#top)

**Backup and restore: agreed loss bounds, off-host snapshots and a restore drill**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |

|---|---|
| **Issue** | Preserved proposal 1 of the [architecture reassessment](audits/2026-11-06-architecture-reassessment.md#1-backups-and-recovery-highest-reliability-value): reminders, memory, ledger, enrollment and grant state live in one SQLite database per base; losing the disk loses them. Litestream was dropped with Terminal Dogma, and the recovery outcome was dropped with it. No scheduled encrypted off-host backup and accepted general restore drill exists; one-off lifecycle/root snapshots do not satisfy this feature. |
| **Reproduce** | Remove `~/.nerv` on a disposable base: nothing restores reminders, memory, identity or revoked grants. |
| **Check** | Owner-agreed loss window and restore time; consistent live snapshots (SQLite backup API) on a schedule; retained, encrypted off-host copies with keys kept apart from routine runtime authority; a restore drill onto another location within the agreed bounds that keeps identities, revoked grants and notification checkpoints and replays no old work; no secrets in logs. |

### <a id="f-135"></a>[✨ F-135](#top)

**Watcher of the watcher: the owner hears when the main base goes silent**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🔴 Open | 🔺 P1 | 🔴 Large | 5.75 h agent + 0.5 h owner | — | — | 🤖 | — | — |

💻 **→** Next: F-135-T01 picks the watcher and the silence limit.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Nothing outside the NERV process tells the owner that the main base is down, hung or asleep. launchd restarts a crash (`KeepAlive`, `src/service.ts:61`) but not a hang or a powered-off Mac; the standby bases see missed Kaji heartbeats (`src/kaji-link.ts:212`) but no owner notice was found (search: heartbeat, watchdog, "unreachable"); the threat map row ASI08 still says "partial watchdog" (`docs/security/agentic-threats.md:18`). grover and fpvbuddy alerts also flow through nerv, so a silent main base silences them too. |
| **Reproduce** | With NERV-01 as main and Tabgha as standby: stop the service on NERV-01 (`launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/io.nerv.agent`) or put the Mac to sleep; no message reaches the owner on any channel, however long it stays down. |
| **Check** | When the main base misses heartbeats for the agreed N minutes (hang, stopped service, sleep or power off), a second base sends the owner one notice on Telegram (the one-channel rule lets the standby speak while the main is offline) and one recovery notice when heartbeats return; no repeat per missed beat; a join test across both bases fails first (F-135-T02); with a single base the limit is stated, not hidden; the owner sees it once on the phone (F-135-T04). |

### <a id="b-167"></a>[🐞 B-167](#top)

**Owner requests read in the wrong language, or without their battery tools, before Misato plans**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🟡 Implemented | 🔺 P1 | 🟢 Small | 1 h | — | — | 🤖 | — | — |

💻 **→** Next: B-167-T03 (review findings) in nerv#833; close once it lands on green CI.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Found while building the nerv-planner Gauntlet pack. `requestLanguage` (`src/misato.ts`) reads "quante batterie devo caricare?" and "stampa i piedini di Smoke" as English: the first has no word in its Italian list, and in the second "i" counts as English, so Misato is told to reply in English to the owner's Italian. `detectToolDomains` misses the English plural "batteries" (`batter[iy]\b`), so "how many batteries do I need to charge?" offers no battery tool, even after `tools.read` with subject batteries. |
| **Reproduce** | `node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./src/misato.ts'); console.log(m.requestLanguage('quante batterie devo caricare?'), m.requestLanguage('stampa i piedini di Smoke'), [...m.detectToolDomains({request:'how many batteries do I need to charge?'})])"` prints `en en []`. |
| **Check** | The three requests read as `it`, `it` and `batteries` (a test fails first, B-167-T01); the fix keeps the existing language and domain tests passing, and nerv-planner is rebuilt (`node tools/gauntlet-planner-pack.mjs`), so its changed cases are pending again (B-167-T02). |

### <a id="b-143"></a>[🐞 B-143](#top)

**A relative reminder time counts from the model step that writes the call, not from when the owner asked**

### <a id="f-144"></a>[✨ F-144](#top)

**Keep the local model warm: longer keep-alive, warm-up at known moments, an optional always-loaded setting**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🔴 Open | 🔶 P2 | 🔴 Large | 6.25 h agent + 0.25 h owner | — | — | 🤖 | — | — |

💻 **→** Next: F-144-T01 — Failing test and probe: how keep&#95;alive reaches Ollama (Planned).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner decision 2026-11-26 in chat: "ollama a+b, c as option in dashboard". The first reply after an idle period is slow because Ollama unloads a model about 5 minutes after its last use and the next request reloads it (gemma4:26b is about 16 GB, gemma4:12b about 8 GB). Three parts: **A** NERV asks Ollama to keep its role models loaded longer after the last use (default 30 minutes, configurable); **B** NERV warms the model at known moments (service start, after an update, about 1 minute before a scheduled brief or reminder that needs it); **C** "keep loaded always" (keep_alive -1) as an owner option in the dashboard Settings, off by default, with a memory warning (a pinned model conflicts with VMs and with ComfyUI image runs, which unload models; the image runner's `--unload-ollama` interplay is [F-144-T06](work/records/F-144.md#f-144)). Plus time to first token, cold against warm, shown in `nerv doctor` and the dashboard so the gain is visible. How NERV calls Ollama today: `src/engine-provider.ts` sends OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` (streamed) and no `keep_alive`; Ollama's `/v1` endpoint may ignore `keep_alive`, so [F-144-T01](work/records/F-144.md#f-144) decides between native `/api/chat` and a prompt-less `/api/generate` with `keep_alive` after each reply. |
| **Reproduce** | Leave NERV idle for more than 5 minutes (`ollama ps` shows the model gone), then send a chat message: the first reply waits for the model to load. |
| **Check** | A request carries the configured `keep_alive` on local Ollama role calls only (T01, T02); the models are loaded after a service start, an update and shortly before a scheduled brief, never blocking a reminder when Ollama is down (T03); "keep loaded always" is off by default, validated, and does not fight an image run (T04, T06); cold and warm time to first token shown in doctor and the dashboard (T05, T07); the owner sees the faster first reply (T08). |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner request 2026-11-25, after [B-144](work/records/F-130.md#b-144). The dashboard in `web/public/dashboard/` is hand-written JavaScript (`index.html` about 48 KB, `live.js` about 135 KB, `dashboard.js` about 126 KB) that rebuilds each section with `innerHTML` on every poll, so unchanged state is redrawn (B-144: EVA images reloaded for nothing). Health and Settings exist only there; the Angular workspace (`web/src`, Angular 22) holds the overview, reminders, doctor and battery cards. Two front ends repeat the same session, pairing and push rules. |
| **Reproduce** | Open `/dashboard/` and `/` on the same service: Health, Settings, sorties, approvals, EVA cages, pilots, comms, the debrief, bases and push exist only in the first, rendered by string building in `live.js` and `dashboard.js`. |
| **Check** | Every dashboard section (at-a-glance strip, Misato's apartment approvals and memory, sorties and plan detail, Sephirot flow, comms and slash commands, debrief, coming up, Health, Settings with devices and pairing, push, models, budget, bases map, chronicle, EVA cages, pilots, tools, skills, Lilith, header chrome) runs in the workspace with the same behaviour, each with a test across the API and the component; an unchanged poll leaves the DOM in place; push taps still post the receipt (F-004-T09); `/dashboard/` and the installed app lead to the workspace and the old files are gone; a simple view (chat, pending approvals, health at a glance, push on/off, a link to the full dashboard) stays beside the full dashboard over the same components and theme tokens; the owner's check of both views on the Mac and the phone. |

### <a id="b-099"></a>[🐞 B-099](#top)

**An EVA-03 job's child in its own session survives the job's timeout and cancellation**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🔴 Open | 🔶 P2 | 🔴 Large | 5.5 h agent + 0.25 h owner | — | [F-049-T14](#f-049-t14) | 🤖 | — | — |

💻 **→** Next: B-099-T02 — EVA jobs can run as a dedicated job user; everything it runs ends with the job (Implemented; verification pending).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Found 2026-11-19 while writing F-049-T05: `runEva03Job` (`src/eva-runner.ts`) kills the job's process group only. A child started in its own session (`spawn(..., { detached: true })`, `setsid`) is outside that group and keeps running after the job timed out or was cancelled; a child in the group is killed. The T01 contract (`docs/decisions/eva-runner.md`, test 5) requires zero surviving processes. EVA execution is not enabled yet, so no live job is affected. |
| **Reproduce** | An EVA-03 job that spawns `node -e "setInterval(()=>{},1000)"` detached, then hangs: after the timeout (or an abort) that child's pid is still alive. |
| **Check** | Test committed failing first: after timeout and after cancellation no process the job started is alive, including one in its own session (B-099-T01). Owner decision 2026-11-19: track descendants while the job runs; a survivor is recorded as an uncertain effect, never as a clean end. Owner decision 2026-11-19 after review: tracking is best effort and every EVA-03 event says so; a boundary the job cannot leave (a dedicated job user) follows in B-099-T02. |

### <a id="b-066"></a>[🐞 B-066](#top)

**Worker-link heartbeat verification awaits nervous SQLite IPC on every frame**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🔴 Open | 🔶 P2 | 🟢 Small | 0.75 h | — | — | 🤖 | — | — |

💻 **→** Next: B-066-T02 — Decouple worker-link frame verification from per-frame nervous IPC (Implemented; verification pending).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | `Peer.receive` in `src/worker-link.ts` awaits `registry.bases()` and `registry.main()` on the serial `this.incoming` chain for every frame, making four `nervous` SQLite IPC calls per `worker.ping` round-trip in `serve` (`src/runtime.ts`) while `expire()` caps its wait on `this.incoming` at one `timeoutMs`. Under SQLite or IPC contention, an already-received pong stalls behind `nervous` IPC and drops the session, driving repeated timing workarounds in B-046 (PR #293, PR #361) and B-060-T02 ([PR #411](https://github.com/voidbrain/nerv/pull/411)). |
| **Reproduce** | Compare the options in [worker heartbeat liveness](decisions/worker-heartbeat-liveness.md), or run `test/worker-link.test.ts` (`B-046`) with a 150 ms heartbeat budget when `nervous` IPC latency exceeds `timeoutMs / 2`. |
| **Check** | Owner chooses Option A (in-memory registry snapshot inside `WorkerLink`, invalidated on registry changes) or Option B (decouple socket arrival liveness from the async `nervous` IPC queue); B-066-T02 implements the chosen design and adds a slow-registry regression in `test/worker-link.test.ts` (restoring a tight budget there). |

### <a id="f-087"></a>[✨ F-087](#top)

**3D printing: slice a model with a material profile and send it to the printer**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |

🧑 **→** Next: [🧑‍🔧](decisions/bambu-print-handoff.md) F-087-T04 — Owner check on the real printer (Planned).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner job 2026-11-14: "print that STL with PLA settings". The owner's printer takes jobs from other software only through the vendor's desktop app (Bambu Connect, Bambu Lab's official path for third-party tools). Starting a print or reading its status from outside needs the firmware's Developer Mode, which is LAN-only and disconnects the printer from the vendor cloud. So NERV prepares and hands off the job; the owner presses Print in the app. The signed-in vendor app runs on Tabgha (NERV-02, Windows 11), where NERV runs as a background service with no window: the job goes to Tabgha (F-050), and opening the app needs the owner's logged-in desktop session. |
| **Reproduce** | Ask to print an STL with a named material. |
| **Check** | The model is sliced with a named material profile (Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer, on the base that has the app); time and material are reported; the sliced file opens in Bambu Connect (`bambu-connect://import-file` link) with a checklist for the owner (printer, plate, nozzle, filament and AMS mapping, clear plate, someone nearby for the first layer); NERV never reports a print as started, because it cannot see the printer; an unknown profile is refused. Developer Mode control is out of scope unless the owner chooses it in T01. |

|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner approved 2026-11-25. On the owner's Mac (M3 Pro, 36 GB, load average 8–15), with a 3,900-token prompt and uncached prompt reading, gemma4:26b read the prompt about twice as fast as gemma4:12b and generated faster: gemma4:12b 200 tok/s reading, 37 tok/s generation; gemma4:26b 441 / 45; qwen3-coder:30b 565 / 35; qwen2.5-coder:14b 168 / 13; devstral-small-2:24b 99 / 7; gemma4:e2b about 3,000 / 50. The cost is memory: about 16 GB against 8 GB for gemma4:12b. Prompt reading matters because every "(invalid reply)" retry (B-136) re-reads the whole prompt. ### <a id="f-142"></a>[✨ F-142](#top)

**Vision in chat: the owner sends an image and a local model understands it**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🟣 Blocked | ◻️ P3 | 🔴 Large | 7.75 h agent + 0.25 h owner | — | — | 🤖 | — | 🤔 |

🧑 **→** Parked: waits for the owner to pick a use; [candidate uses](work/records/F-142.md).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner decision 2026-11-26 in chat on fpvbuddy:F-023: "A" (retire the on-device assistant and the vision demo), with "vision capabilities ideally on nerv too". Today a photo sent to NERV is only attached to a recipe, crash, part or battery by caption (`src/telegram.ts`); NERV cannot say what an image shows. `gemma4:12b` (local, Ollama) accepts images. The owner uses NERV in Italian. **Parked:** Owner decision in chat 2026-11-26: "park F-142 with its possible uses". Candidate uses, the owner picks one (or none) before any step starts: (a) a photo of a handwritten or printed recipe becomes a NERV recipe; (b) a photo of a battery label fills battery details (FPVBuddy over MCP); (c) a plant photo gets a health check (Grover); (d) check that a web image really shows the requested place or item before offering it ([F-143](work/records/F-142.md#f-143)). Attaching an image to a recipe or place ("usa questa") needs no vision and no longer depends on this record. |
| **Reproduce** | Send a photo without an attach caption on Telegram: NERV replies with the caption help. The PWA chat has no way to send an image; `POST /api/chat` takes text only. |
| **Check** | A photo sent on Telegram, the PWA or `/api/chat` is answered in the owner's language (Italian by default) by a local vision model only (F-142-T02, T03, T05); images stay local, EXIF/GPS stripped, size and type limits, a retention sweep (T03); text read from an image is tainted, never an instruction, and cannot alone propose or approve a tool (T04); NERV Gauntlet cases in Italian and English (T06) and the model qualified on a Gauntlet vision pack (T07, needs gauntlet-protocol work); the owner checks it on Telegram and the PWA (T08). |
